features.text: The patient has been experiencing back pain on the left side for a while.
The back pain is worse when bending over.
The back pain is random and not constant.
Stretching usually helps alleviate the back pain.
The patient has no numbness, tingling, or weakness in the legs or feet associated with the back pain.
The patient had a microdiscectomy in November 2020 due to a herniated disc that wrapped around the spinal thecal sac.
The patient experienced nerve pain down the leg and back after the surgery and was on a high dose of gabapentin.
The patient had an X-ray taken during the current visit, which showed no fractures or spinal bone issues and indicated proper healing of the surgery site.
The pain is located on the left side of the lower back, near the surgery site.
The back pain does not radiate to the legs.
The patient has not had any MRI or CT scans of the lumbar spine since the 2020 microdiscectomy.
The patient is open to considering an MRI or CT scan if it would help determine the cause of the current back pain.
The patient has not been consistently following physical therapy recommendations, including stretching and strengthening exercises.
The patient has not experienced any new or worsening neurological symptoms since the microdiscectomy.
The duration of the current back pain is uncertain but likely several months.
The back pain is more likely to occur during active periods, especially when bending over.
